name: MAEL (Multi-Agent cross-task Experiential Learning)
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2505.23187, cs.CL; marked 'Work in Progress'); not yet peer-reviewed
authors_affiliation: Yilong Li (Peking University), Chen Qian (Shanghai Jiao Tong University), Yu Xia, Ruijie Shi, Yufan Dang, Zihao Xie, Weize Chen, Zhiyuan Liu, Maosong Sun (Tsinghua University), Ziming You (Peking University), Cheng Yang (Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications), Weichuan Liu (Siemens), Ye Tian, Xuantang Xiong, Lei Han (Tencent Robotics X). Equal contribution: Yilong Li, Chen Qian. Corresponding authors: Zhiyuan Liu, Maosong Sun.
code_url: N/A (no official code repository is referenced in the paper or located via search) [uncertain]
task_domain: Multi-agent LLM collaboration spanning QA/multi-domain reasoning (MMLU), arithmetic reasoning (GSM-8K), code synthesis (HumanEval), long-form/commonsense generation (CommonGen-Hard), and project-level software development / code generation (SRDD). General task-solving with decomposition + critique rather than a single domain.
problem_setting: Interactive, multi-agent (graph of N LLM agents on an undirected collaboration network). Two-phase: an offline-style 'experiential learning phase' over a training corpus (30 training tasks per dataset) where reward annotations are computed per decision step, followed by an inference phase on held-out tasks. Supervision is available during the learning phase via task-specific reward/metric functions (e.g., accuracy, pass@k, composite quality scores). Each agent maintains its own distributed experience pool. The setting is cross-task transfer: learning from previously solved tasks to improve future structurally-similar tasks.
what_is_retrieved: Per-agent past 'experiences' = step-level input-output pairs annotated with a quality reward, of the form (state s_t, action a_t, reward r_t), used as few-shot examples. At task-wise granularity, a complete high-quality solution trace is retrieved.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING / episodic memory the agents write. Each agent's experience pool is built (induced) during the experiential learning phase from the system's own collaboration traces; it is not a static external corpus/KB.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking (effectively top-1): the single top-ranked experience entry by the combined similarity-and-reward retrieval score is appended to the agent input. No notion of recovering a complete minimal set or precision-driven variable size.
retrieval_unit: (state, action, reward) tuple = a single agent input-output pair annotated with a quality reward (step-level experience). Under task-wise retrieval the unit is a full high-quality solution trace for the task; under step-wise retrieval the unit is the per-decision-step experience tuple.
index_source: Growing memory induced online during a dedicated experiential learning (training) phase from the multi-agent system's own forward-pass collaboration traces over a 30-task training set per dataset; experiences are accumulated incrementally over the training dataset. Frozen at inference (no write-back at test time noted).
index_structure_topology: Distributed per-agent flat experience pools: each agent (node v_i) owns its own pool p_i organized as a flat collection of (s,a,r) entries searched by embedding similarity. The agents themselves are organized on an undirected graph collaboration network, but the retrievable store within each agent is a flat vector-keyed index.
retriever_type: Dense embedding retriever (cosine similarity over text-embedding-ada-002 embeddings) combined with a reward weighting; off-the-shelf embedder, not learned.
retriever_learning_signal: None for the embedder itself (off-the-shelf text-embedding-ada-002). The ranking signal is a hand-designed weighted combination of cosine similarity and the stored task-effectiveness reward (downstream step quality), retrieval_score = alpha*similarity + (1-alpha)*reward with alpha=0.5 by default. The reward component is derived from task-specific downstream quality metrics, so selection is biased by downstream-task-effectiveness but the retriever is not trained.
query_construction: Raw agent input at the current decision step (the subtask description / state s_t) is embedded and used as the query. For task-wise retrieval the original task description is used as the query for the whole task; for step-wise retrieval each step's input is the query.
query_granularity: Both supported as variants: task-level one-shot query (MAEL_Task, query = original task description, applied throughout the task) and step/state-level query (MAEL_Step, a fresh query at each decision step).
when_to_retrieve: Variant-dependent: one-shot at task start (MAEL_Task) or iterative per-decision-step (MAEL_Step). Retrieval happens on a fixed schedule at each agent decision step, not uncertainty-triggered or learned-router gated.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval is performed deterministically at each critical decision step (task solve, solvability judge, task decompose, solution critique, solution aggregate) for MAEL_Step, or once at task start for MAEL_Task. No confidence/uncertainty/learned-classifier trigger.
reranking: No separate neural reranking stage; ranking is a single weighted-scoring step combining cosine similarity and stored reward (a similarity+reward weighted score), then top-1 selection.
retrieved_context_refinement: None beyond the similarity+reward scoring and top-1 selection; the retrieved experience entry is appended verbatim to the agent input. No decomposition/distillation/compression/distractor-filtering of retrieved context is described.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: the top-ranked experience (s_j, a_j, r_j) is appended to the agent input s_t as a few-shot example, and the augmented input is fed to the agent to generate the response. It guides subtask decomposition strategy and inter-agent communication/solving/refinement/aggregation.
planning_integration: Per-step interleaved within a divide-and-conquer + solver-critique collaboration workflow. Retrieval is woven into each stage of the recursive task-solving workflow (Decompose -> Solve -> Critique -> Aggregate); experiences guide both task decomposition and inter-agent communication. This is a retrieve-at-each-step (MAEL_Step) or retrieve-once-then-plan (MAEL_Task) integration, not inside an explicit MCTS/tree search.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-decision-step / per-agent-action within a collaboration rollout (for MAEL_Step), i.e., retrieval at each of the workflow's critical decision steps (decompose, solve, critique, aggregate). For MAEL_Task it is per-task (one retrieval reused across the whole rollout).
retrieved_item_representation: Raw stored input-output trajectory pair (state-action text) annotated with a numeric reward, injected as a free-text few-shot exemplar; under task-wise retrieval it is the raw historical solution trace. Not distilled into abstract rules or executable skills.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw trajectory / raw demonstration (a concrete past input-output pair or full solution trace), not a distilled strategy, abstract guideline, or procedural skill.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Reward-weighted similarity scoring biases retrieval toward high-quality (high-reward) and relevant experiences, providing implicit robustness. The paper empirically reports robustness: even Low-Reward & Low-Similarity retrieval still beats no-experience (e.g., +6.7% on HumanEval), but there is no explicit relevance-evaluator, self-reflection filter, or retriever-aware training to guard against noise.
memory_type: Episodic (per-agent distributed experience pools of (state, action, reward) interaction traces); analogized to learnable weights of a neural-network-like agent graph.
write_back: True (during the experiential learning phase). Agents store new (s_t, a_t, r_t) experiences into their individual experience pools via a backpropagation-style backward pass: P <- P union {(s_t,a_t,r_t)}. However, write-back occurs only in the dedicated training/learning phase, not during test-time inference.
online_growth: Partial / No at deployment. The store grows incrementally during the experiential learning phase over the training set, but appears frozen during the inference (test) phase (inference retrieves from the pool 'constructed in the experiential learning phase'). No test-time growth is described. [uncertain] whether any inference-time write-back occurs.
write_back_trigger: On every traversed critical decision step during the learning-phase forward/backward pass (per-step), regardless of success or failure. Each step's (input, output, reward) is stored after the forward pass computes its reward; storage is reward-annotated but not gated on success only. Effectively per-step write during training.
failure_experience_usage: Experiences are stored with their rewards including low-reward (lower-quality) ones, not success-only; the reward annotation lets retrieval prefer high-reward experiences. The paper analyzes 'Low Reward' vs 'High Reward' retrieval, showing low-reward experiences still help, but there is no explicit failure-only corrective-rule mechanism or contrastive success/failure usage; failures are simply stored as low-reward entries and down-weighted at retrieval.
memory_evolution_update: Append-only: experiences are accumulated (P <- P union {(s_t,a_t,r_t)}) over the training set. No dedup-merge, delta-update, refine-overwrite, or forgetting/pruning of stored entries is described.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval/case-selection is a fixed similarity+reward weighted top-1 scoring rule (alpha=0.5), not a learned/RL-optimized retrieval policy. The framing uses RL-like terms (state, action, reward, forward/backward pass) but the experience pools act as non-parametric 'weights' and the retriever is not trained.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Per-agent private memory: each agent (node) maintains its own individual/distributed experience pool; experiences are NOT pooled into a shared global memory across agents. Sharing across heterogeneous frameworks is not addressed. Coordination is via the graph edges, but experience pools are agent-specific.
benchmarks: MMLU; GSM-8K (GSM); HumanEval; CommonGen-Hard; SRDD (Software Requirement Description Dataset, project-level software development).
benchmark_family: QA/multi-domain knowledge (MMLU); arithmetic reasoning (GSM-8K); code (HumanEval function-level; SRDD project/repository-level software development); long-form/commonsense generation (CommonGen-Hard). No standard web/embodied/tool/memory-RL benchmark families used.
baselines: Single-agent: GPT-4o-mini, Claude-3.5-sonnet. Multi-agent: AutoGen (Wu et al. 2023), EvoMac/EvoMAC (Hu et al. 2025). Internal variants: MAEL_NoExp (no experience), MAEL_Task (task-wise retrieval), MAEL_Step (step-wise retrieval).
key_metrics: Accuracy (MMLU, GSM-8K); pass@k (HumanEval); official composite metric for CommonGen-Hard (grammar, fluency, relevance, logical consistency, concept coverage); SRDD quality = product of completeness, executability, consistency. Efficiency: completion token consumption and number of convergence rounds/dialogue turns. Also code-scale metrics (cyclomatic complexity, lines, tokens, functions, files).
headline_result: MAEL outperforms single-/multi-agent baselines on most of 5 datasets; average score: MAEL_NoExp 65.67, MAEL_Task 69.69, MAEL_Step 66.52 vs GPT-4o-mini 60.78 and AutoGen 55.18. On SRDD, MAEL_Step quality 76.43 (+20.21% over AutoGen baseline, +9.2% over MAEL_NoExp) and reduces average dialogue rounds to convergence by 26%. On CommonGen-Hard, MAEL_Task cuts token usage by 49% vs MAEL_NoExp while improving quality by 12.04 points (new SOTA). (Default backbone: GPT-3.5, temperature 0.2, 4-node topology, 30 training tasks per dataset.)
ablations: (1) Three retrieval strategies compared (No-Exp / Task-wise / Step-wise) across all datasets and on SRDD quality breakdown; MAEL_Step best on SRDD, MAEL_Task best on average. (2) Factors-affecting-retrieval ablation (Table 4): 2x2 of High/Low Similarity x High/Low Reward on HumanEval and CommonGen — both factors help individually; combining High Reward & High Similarity gives largest gain (HumanEval 73.3->90.0, +12.5% relative; CommonGen +10.1%); even Low&Low beats no-experience (+6.7% on HumanEval). (3) Experience-pool scaling (Fig 3): performance vs pool size (0/10/20/30 tasks) on HumanEval (76.7->90.0, non-monotonic dip at 20) and CommonGen (34.5->46.5). (4) Efficiency analysis (Fig 2): token consumption and convergence rounds reductions. (5) Code scale/complexity metrics (Table 3). Note experience hurts slightly on MMLU and GSM (low solution overlap / low complexity).
evaluation_decoupling: No. Intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / completeness of retrieval) are NOT reported separately; evaluation is end-to-end task performance plus the similarity/reward-factor ablation, but retrieval quality is measured only through downstream task scores.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both. Outcome: task accuracy/pass@k/quality. Process: number of convergence rounds / dialogue turns to converge, token consumption per inference, per-step solution-quality progression over iterations (case study Fig 4), and intermediate SRDD sub-metrics (completeness, executability, consistency) plus code-scale/complexity statistics.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Reported. Experience retrieval reduces completion-token consumption and convergence rounds across nearly all datasets: CommonGen-Hard MAEL_Task cuts token usage 49% vs MAEL_NoExp (with +12.04 quality); SRDD MAEL_Step reduces average dialogue rounds to convergence by 26% (with +9.25 quality). Values normalized relative to MAEL_NoExp for SRDD due to its much higher cost. Retrieval cost itself (embedding/lookup) not separately quantified.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed top-1 selection: the single top-ranked experience entry is appended to the agent input as a few-shot example (top-k=1). Workflow budget controlled via fixed hyperparameters: max refinement rounds 2 (simple: MMLU/HumanEval/GSM) or 3 (complex: CommonGen-Hard/SRDD), and max task-decomposition layers 1 or 2 respectively; 4-node topology; 30 training tasks per dataset. No explicit token-budget cap on injected context described.
builds_on: ChatDev / Experiential Co-Learning (Qian et al. 2024a,b) for software-developing agents and graph/linear MAS workflows; AutoGen (Wu et al. 2023) and AgentVerse/CAMEL/MetaGPT MAS frameworks; EvoMAC (Hu et al. 2025) self-evolving MAS (also a baseline); Self-Refine (Madaan et al. 2023, also source of CommonGen-Hard) for iterative critique; ExpeL (Zhao et al. 2024) 'LLM agents are experiential learners' for experience accumulation; neural-network/backpropagation analogy (forward/backward pass).
contrasts_with: Myopic MAS frameworks that solve each task from scratch without cross-task transfer (AutoGen, AgentVerse, CAMEL, MetaGPT). Self-evolving MAS that adapt topologies at test-time without a dedicated experience-accumulation training phase (EvoMAC/Hu et al. 2025; EvoFlow/Zhang et al. 2025). MAEL distinguishes itself by (a) a dedicated training phase accumulating historical cross-task experience and (b) assigning fine-grained step-level rewards to each experience for reward-weighted retrieval.
lineage: Group D (case-based / experiential planning): experience/case-based planners that learn from prior task episodes. Sits in the lineage of experience-accumulation agents (ExpeL, Reflexion, Experiential Co-Learning / ChatDev) extended to graph-structured multi-agent collaboration with per-agent reward-weighted episodic retrieval; positioned within the self-evolving MAS line (vs EvoMAC) but emphasizing offline cross-task experiential learning rather than test-time topology evolution.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Retrieve: yes (reward-weighted similarity retrieval of past experiences). Reuse: yes (injected as few-shot exemplars guiding decomposition/communication). Revise: partial (the workflow has a critique/refinement loop that revises current solutions, but retrieved cases are not explicitly adapted/revised before reuse — they are used verbatim). Retain: yes (write-back of new (s,a,r) experiences during the learning phase). 4-flag: [Retrieve=Yes, Reuse=Yes, Revise=Partial, Retain=Yes].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work does NOT frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner; it frames experiences via a neural-network/backpropagation analogy (agents as neurons, experience pools as learnable weights, forward/backward passes) and the term 'experiential learning'. It realizes CBR-like retrieve-reuse-retain mechanics under a different framing.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tool/skill retrieval; experiences are agent interaction traces, not tool documents).
index_content_separation: N/A (no lightweight-index-vs-heavy-content separation; experiences are stored and retrieved as whole (s,a,r) entries / traces).
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool index or tool-integration protocol; not a tool-retrieval method).
adaptation_mechanism: Verbatim ICL exemplar: the top-ranked retrieved experience is appended unchanged to the agent input as a few-shot example (no explicit LLM-prompted adaptation, execution-feedback revision, or RL reuse-finetuning of the retrieved case itself). Solution revision happens via the separate solver-critique refinement loop, not by adapting the retrieved case.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (not a benchmark paper; reuses existing datasets — MMLU, GSM-8K, HumanEval, CommonGen-Hard, SRDD — with 30 training tasks per dataset and an evaluation/test split; exact test-set sizes per dataset not specified in the paper). [uncertain]
